deep.reconstruction:
Folio 219 (also numbered 111) has no written derivation. The faint rows of numbers across the upper two-thirds are mirror-image show-through from the facing page. Their columns match the logarithmic computations on the next page (e.g. 4.1743088 - 7472, 5.5596674 + 7913, +0.3919916, +1.1657552), so they are not text belonging to this page. The only original ink is a pen diagram:
- a long vertical line near the right edge;
- two horizontal lines, an upper one at about two-thirds of the page height and a lower one about 250 px below it, both crossing the vertical line;
- a two-segment broken line. It starts on the upper horizontal line at a point marked '3' and runs down to the right with a long, gently sloping segment. That segment carries tick marks labelled '3', '2' and '1' (the '1' sits just left of where it crosses the lower horizontal line). It continues below the lower line to a lowest point. From there a short, steep segment rises to meet the vertical line between the two horizontals.
- Labels '3', '2' (at the upper-line crossing) and '1' are written along the vertical line, plus a small mark below the lower line.

No equation, value or text explains the figure, so its purpose can only be conjectured. The previous page is a Fourier-type expansion for an orbit of eccentricity 0.9. The next page solves the trinomial x^7 - 3x^2 - 0.3598223 = 0, written there as x^7 - e x^2 + f = 0. It uses Gauss's trigonometric substitution x = r(cos R + i sin R), with lambda = sin(2R)^2 sin(5R)^5 / sin(7R)^7 and r^5 = e sin(7R)/sin(5R). The next page also writes r^7 = -f sin 2R / sin 5R; that expression should properly carry sin 7R in the denominator (see errors).

The imaginary part of the equation gives r^5 sin 7R = e sin 2R. The real part then gives a law-of-sines relation among r^7, e r^2 and f, with angles 7R, 2R and 5R. A broken line or triangle diagram illustrating that vector relation, or the number of roots by angular sector, would fit the next page. This is my conjecture and cannot be verified from the image. Nothing on this page can be reconstructed as a derivation.
errors: No computational content on this page to check.

Context (next page, not this page): the relation transcribed as r^7 = -f sin2R/sin5R should, from the trinomial theory, carry sin7R in the denominator (r^7 sin7R = f sin 2R type relation, up to sign convention); likely a transcription slip or shorthand.
Context check of the next page: the roots found sum to about -7e-7, i.e. essentially 0 as required by the missing x^6 term. This confirms that page's computations.

results.what: Unlabelled geometric diagram (broken line between two parallel horizontals and a vertical axis, with tick labels 1-3), probably an auxiliary figure for the trigonometric solution of the trinomial x^7 - e x^2 + f = 0 on the adjacent page.
results.modern_name: Geometric/polygon representation of the roots of a trinomial equation (conjectural)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Beiträge zur Theorie der algebraischen Gleichungen (1849), for the trigonometric treatment of trinomial equations

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds only an unexplained sketch plus show-through from the facing page. The associated trinomial-equation method is published Gauss material (1849).
